Document.project_name: North Corridor Expansion Project
Document.description: NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd. (NGTL) is applying to the National Energy Board under section 52 of the National Energy Board Act for approval to construct and operate the North Corridor Expansion Project (the Project) in Alberta.  The Project consists of three natural gas pipelines: two sections of 1,219 mm (nominal pipe size 48 inch), including the 24 km long North Star Section 2 and the 32 km long Red Earth Section 3, and a third section of 1,219 mm (nominal pipe size 36 inch) which is 25 km long and called the Bear Canyon North Extension on the Northwest Mainline Loop No.2.  The Project also includes a unit addition at Hidden Lake North Compressor Station and launcher and receiver facilities for cleaning and in-line inspection. Temporary infrastructure required for construction could include temporary access roads, borrow pits/dugouts, slurry pits, stockpile sites, laydown yards, contractor yards and construction camps. The Project will cross 6 watercourses located in the Peace River Basin; named watercourses include the Notikewin River, Loon River, Hunt Creek, and Bear Canyon Creek. NGTL is proposing to commence construction at the compressor station in November 2019 and commence all three pipeline sections from September 2021 to April 2022.

Document.project_name: Edson Mainline Expansion Project
Document.description: NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd. (NGTL) is applying to the National Energy Board under section 52 of the National Energy Board Act for approval to construct and operate the Edson Mainline Expansion Project (the Project) in Alberta.  The Project consists of two sections of 1,219 mm (nominal pipe size 48) natural gas pipeline, including the 40.2 km long Elk River Section and the 44.7 km long Alford Creek Section, and associated facilities.  The associated facilities include three mainline block valves, one control valve and bypass assembly, ten crossover valves, a receiver facility, and temporary access roads.  The Project will cross 31 watercourses located in the North Saskatchewan River watershed, notably the Brazeau River, Nordegg River, Elk River, Prairie Creek, and the Clearwater River.  NGTL is proposing to construct both pipeline sections from November 2021 to April 2022.

Document.project_name: NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd. - 2021 NGTL System Expansion Project
Document.description:
NOVA Gas Transmission Limited (NGTL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Trans Canada, has filed an application for the 2021 NGTL System Expansion Project. NGTL proposes to build and operate approximately 344 km of 1,219 mm (NPS 48) outside diameter natural gas pipeline and associated facilities in northwestern Alberta. If approved, the project would "loop" or add new pipeline parallel or adjacent to, the existing NGTL System.

The Project includes three main areas:

Grande Prairie West Area:


	Grande Prairie Mainline Loop No. 4 (Valhalla Section), approximately 36 km; and,
	Grande Prairie Mainline Loop No. 3 (Elmworth Section), approximately 46 km.


Grande Prairie South Area:


	Grande Prairie Mainline Loop No. 2 (Karr Section), approximately 57 km;
	Grande Prairie Mainline Loop No. 2 (Deep Valley Section), approximately 69 km; and,
	Grande Prairie Mainline Loop No. 2 (McLeod River Connection Section), approximately 14 km.


Edson South Area:


	Edson Mainline Loop No. 4 (Rob Section), approximately 42 km;
	Edson Mainline Loop No. 4 (Dismal Creek Section), approximately 32 km;
	Edson Mainline Loop 4 (Brewer Section), approximately 49 km;
	Three compressor station unit additions at Nordegg, AB, Didsbury, AB and Beiseker, AB; and,
	January Creek Control Valve and associated pipeline tie-ins.


In its application, NGTL said the project was needed to transport natural gas from areas of increasing production in northwestern Alberta and northeastern BC to intra-Alberta and export markets. If approved, NGTL plans to begin operating the project by April 2021.

The application includes designated physical activities listed in the Regulations Designating Physical Activities (Regulations) under the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act, 2012 (CEAA 2012), specifically the construction of over 40 km of new pipeline. As a result, the Project will be a designated project for the purposes of CEAA 2012 for which the NEB will be the responsible authority.

Document.project_name: Cold Lake First Nation: CUZ46 Wastewater System Expansion
Document.description:
The existing capacity of the Cold Lake First Nation wastewater collection and treatment system has been deemed insufficient to meet current and projected future demand. As such, Cold Lake First Nation proposes the expansion of its wastewater collection infrastructure to include an expansion of the collection system, and construction of a new lift station, 4.4 km of wastewater forcemain and gravity wastewater main, connection to the City of Cold Lake wastewater collection and treatment infrastructure, and decommissioning of the existing Cold Lake First Nation wastewater treatment lagoon. The on-reserve portions of the routing will generally follow established roadways to the crossing of the Beaver River.

     Extensive geohazard analysis and geotechnical investigations have been completed and identified the presence of a deep-seated landslide along the south embankment of the Beaver River. Trees within the landslide area suggest that the slope has not been subject to significant displacement for at least 50 years indicating stability of the area in comparison to other alignments reviewed as part of the project. The north side of the river valley does not demonstrate significant geohazards.

     Vegetation will be cleared and mulched to a width of 4.0m along the entire route to facilitate equipment access and maintenance of the infrastructure.

     The off-reserve alignments generally follow un-developed public right-of-ways under the jurisdiction of the MD of Bonnyville and are outside of the scope of this impact assessment.

Document.project_name: Heart Lake First Nation: CU370 Wastewater System Emergency Repairs
Document.description: Heart Lake First Nation is completing emergency repairs to its wastewater systems infrastructure associated with the band administration offices and community center. Repairs to the system include construction of upgraded sanitary lines (214.6 m of 200 mm PVC pipe, 79.0 m of 150 mm PVC pipe, and 27.24 m of 50 mm HDPE low pressure sanitary main), construction of three new 1200 mm manholes, and upgrades to the water treatment plant filter and analyzer components. The intended repairs will be tied-in to the existing manholes and sanitary service lines. The work requires clearing and grubbing of approx. 0.15 ha of natural forest area to accommodate trenched installation of the upgraded sanitary line.

Document.project_name: Cold Lake First Nation: CUZD3 Phase II and III Water Distribution System
Document.description: Cold Lake First Nation proposes to construct and operate Phase II and Phase III of its water distribution system on its lands at Cold Lake IR No. 149B. Phase II and III will consist of approximately 16 km water distribution main with service to approximately 50 homes. The water system will extend from existing service provided by the City of Cold Lake with line diameter ranging from 250 mm at the connection point to 100 mm at the branch extensions. The watermain network will cross several waterbodies including streams, lakes, and wetlands using horizontal directional drilling methods. Lines will be installed adjacent to existing roads where possible, with segments crossing through undeveloped forested areas of reserve. Vegetation clearing will be completed as necessary to support construction activities, access, and infrastructure components.

Document.project_name: CU472: Tthebatthi De¨ne´suline´ Nation Band Administration & CFS Community Building
Document.description: Tthebatthi De¨ne´suline´ Nation proposes the construction and operation of a new Band Administration & Child & Family Services Community Building on its lands at Thabacha Nare IR No. 196A. The proposed location consists of a cleared lot which was recently added to reserve and was previously used for as a wildland wildfire rapid attack base of operations. The building design includes a 1,783 square meter structure and a total building site footprint of 15,575 square meters. The facility will feature a dedicated outdoor gathering space and fire pit, designated Elder's parking stalls, accessible circulation, and areas intended to support community, family, administrative, and cultural activities.

Document.project_name: YUL Montréal-Trudeau International Airport - Addition of Above-Ground Fuel Storage Tanks at the YUL Garage
Chief Kinosew Awasak Mikiwahp Community Subdivision Development
Document.description:
Chief Kinosew Awasak Mikiwahp, in partnership with Driftpile Cree Nation proposes the development of a new residential subdivision at Driftpile River IR No. 150. The subdivision will include greefield development of new roads, water / wastewater / electrical / gas utilities, drainage infrastructure and storwater pond, lighting, flood mitigation berms, and buildings including a family enhancement building, Mihataakaw Sipiy Law and Governance Lodge, Food Sovereignty Program site, vehicle and storage garage, Child and Family Services building, cultural revitalization lodge, ceremonial cultural space, employee housing, and an independent living four-plex building.

The project will require vegetation clearing, grubbing, grading, excavation, import of fill, construction, construction, paving, and operation. The site has been selected for its core access to the community and connectiong to existing roads.

Document.project_name: Duncan's First Nation: CUCJ0 - Solid Waste Transfer Station
Bigstone Cree Nation: P057828 - Maskotehk Flood Mitigation Upgrades at Cattleman Drive & Cee Too Drive
Document.description: Bigstone Cree Nation proposes the replacement of a watercourse crossing over an unnamed creek in Wabasca IR No. 166D to increase capacity and amelierate flooding issues. Construction will include isolation of the crossing location, installation of a temporary bypass crossing, removal of the existing corssing, installation of a new crossing, removal of the temporary bypass route, and commissioning of the new watercourse crossing.

Document.project_name: Yellowhead Copper Project
Document.description:
Trekor Metals Limited is proposing the construction, operation, and closure of a new open-pit copper mine located about 150 kilometres northeast of Kamloops, British Columbia. The Yellowhead Copper Project has been designed with a production capacity of 90,000 tonnes of ore per day (up to 32 million tonnes per year) over a 25-year mine life. The project, which would also produce gold and silver, includes a new mill, an approximately 110 kilometre transmission line that would connect to an existing B.C. Hydro substation near 100 Mile House, and a rail load-out facility at an existing site at Vavenby.

British Columbia's Environmental Assessment Office is collaborating with the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada as part of the federal impact assessment of the project. For more information on the EAO's process, please visit EPIC.engage.

 

Please note that the proponent of this project was previously known as Taseko Mines Limited.

Document.project_name: Generator and Storage Tank Replacement
Document.description:
This project involves the replacement of 4 Storage tanks and 2 generators (diesel), as well as all associated piping, that make up an EC registered storage tank system at the Little Gold Border Crossing:

Two (2) prime diesel generators and associated power electronics

Two (2) day storage tanks (located inside in the utility building, serving generators, and a fire pump) One (1) day tank (located exterior east side of customs building, for heating)

One (1) main storage tank 20,000 L.

The three day tanks are to be replaced with like-for-like capacity tanks. The main storage tank will be replaced with a slightly larger tank (25,000L) that will be seismically restrained on a new concrete housekeeping pad, in the same location as the previous tank. The new portable generators will be installed outside on a new housekeeping pad, east of the utility building.

The system is all above ground - no subsurface material expected to be disturbed. Design and Installation will adhere to all applicable codes, standards and Federal legislation.

Document.project_name: Septic Tank Decommissioning
Document.description:
Decommissioning of the existing Septic Holding tank for the brick and mortar building

following all environmental regulations:

- Install environmental protection

- Remove contaminated substances from within the septic tank

- Scan for utilities

- Excavate soils to expose structure

- Remove structure

- Backfill area and install pavements where disturbed

 

Note: The site has possible soil contamination. Moreover, there is a high chance of groundwater contamination due to leaching from the septic tank.

Document.project_name: Remediation of mould in Residences 2 & 4
Document.description:
The purpose of this project is to perform mould remediation in the basements of residences 2 & 4.

Remediate Drywall within the basement area 2 feet upwards from the floor for total perimeter of the room in Residence 2. Remediate plywood and underlying drywall within the basement mechanical room 2 feet upwards from the floor where remaining on the perimeter wall and behind the boiler in residence 4. Air scrubber to remain in place for 48 hours following remediation activities. The heating oil storage tank system registered with Environment Canada in duplex 3/4 will likely need to be moved to access the wall behind for remedial work. An electrician, oil burner mechanic and mechanical engineer will need to be present to assist with the work.

Document.project_name: Site Preparation for Trailer Install
Document.description:
BGIS to prepare site for installation of 24X50 trailer, which will be purchased by CBSA and supplied by Corcan.  Considerations for AODA requirements to be included in site design. Below-grade works/excavation is expected (organics and PHC's have been identified and reported on the Federal Contaminated Sites Inventory), and it is required that a mitigation measures form be completed with a focus on this topic.

The project cannot be excluded through the Designated Classes of Project Order when subsurface contamination is reported.

Physical works involved:

- In order to level the site in preparation for a spot for the trailer to sit, excavation is expected.

- Above-grade electrical service will be run from the main building to the trailer.

- Below-grade plumbing service will be run from the main building to the trailer.

Paterson Port of Entry Redevelopment
Rock Bay Harbour Ferry Project - Dredging and Dock Construction
15-Mile Processing Hub Project
Document.description: 15-Mile Minerals and Renewables Ltd. is proposing to construct, operate, decommission and reclaim three historic open-pit gold mines, located 85 to 145 kilometres northeast of Halifax, Nova Scotia. As proposed, the 15-Mile Processing Hub Project would consist of the 15-Mile Mine site (formerly the Fifteen Mile Stream Gold Project), Old Austen Mine site (formerly the Beaver Dam Mine Project) and Old Mitchell Mine site (formerly the Cochrane Hill Gold Project). The 15-Mile Mine site would include four open pits, infrastructure to manage water, tailings and other mine waste, and an ore processing plant. The Old Austen Mine and Old Mitchell Mine sites would each include a single open pit, mine waste storage areas, water management, and infrastructure to transport mined material to the 15-Mile Mine site for processing. The project's total ore production and processing capacity would be approximately 8220 tonnes per day over a mine life of about 11 years.

Document.project_name: New Parking Lot – Canadian Forces Housing Agency (CFHA) Residential Portfolio Capital Investment Plan (RPCIP) – Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Halifax, Windsor
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. DND is proposing construction of a new permanent asphalt parking lot behind Building WP38 (6545 MacDougall Avenue) at Windsor Park, Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Halifax. The project site is located within the Windsor Park military residential community, a developed urban area of Halifax that supports both DND operations and Canadian Forces Housing Agency (CFHA) residential accommodations. The approximately 1,300 m2 lot will provide 29 parking spaces to support CFHA tenants and DND Fire operations. Work includes topsoil stripping, excavation, stormwater tie-in to existing infrastructure, granular base placement and compaction, and asphalt paving. Construction is planned for Summer 2026.

Document.project_name: Stabilization of the banks of Lavoir Creek
location: Forges du Saint-Maurice National Historic Site of Canada
Document.description: During the damage caused by the torrential rains associated with Hurricane Debby in 2024, sandbags were urgently installed to stabilize a section of the banks of Lavoir Creek in the Forge Haute sector of the Forges-du-Saint-Maurice NHS. These sandbags have reached the end of their lifespan and are at risk of deteriorating in the near future. This could lead to increased sediment input into the creek and weaken the stabilization structure. To provide temporary protection for the banks until a permanent solution is implemented, plans are in place to replace the sandbags with a concrete mat. This solution is effective and durable, as it offers greater resistance to weather conditions and erosion. The work will secure the stream banks while providing more adequate protection for the heritage remains. It is also possible that a section located upstream of the work zone—at the junction with the Haut Fourneau Canal—may need to be stabilized, depending on how the situation develops and the project timeline. The planned work involves: Draining the stream during construction. Manually removing sandbags and installing interlocking concrete pavers. Movement of heavy machinery and vehicles (crane, excavator, transport truck, telehandler). Placing sandbags on pallets for transport. Temporary storage of concrete slabs prior to installation. The upstream diversion channel will be used to divert the stream during construction.

Document.project_name: Spruce River Dam Spillway Project
location: Prince Albert National Park of Canada
Document.description: The Spruce River Control Structure, built in 1960 by the Prairie Farm Rehabilitation Administration, regulates flow on the Spruce River and diverts water to Emma Lake and Christopher Lake to maintain recreational water levels. The structure is located about 55 km northwest of Prince Albert, Saskatchewan, near the south end of Anglin Lake. WSA requires the stilling basin and spillway slab to be isolated, dewatered, cleaned, and maintained in inspection-ready condition to support a structural inspection.

Document.project_name: Whistlerville Staff Accommodation Rebuild
Document.description: This project will be assessed with a basic impact assessment. Parks Canada is proposing to rebuild the Whistlerville staff housing units that were lost in the 2024 Jasper Wildfire. The new staff housing units will be located at the south end of the former Marmot Meadows group camp area in Jasper National Park. The housing will be designed for three-season use and will be connected to existing utilities that serve Whistler's Campground and other nearby visitor facilities. The project will restore essential staff housing capacity to support seasonal visitor operations in the park.

Document.project_name: East berth maintenance dredging – Alliance Grain Terminal
location: East berth maintenance dredging - Alliance Grain Terminal
Document.description:
The proposed project is to dredge ~6,500 cubic metres of sediment over a 4,500 square metre area to restore the East berth to the 1995 depths of 13.7 m (45 ft). This berth has not been dredged since 1995, when the pocket was blasted and dredged to increase berth depth for larger vessel access.

Dredging is proposed to be conducted from the water using a barge-mounted crane equipped with a clamshell bucket. Based on sediment characterization at the site, sediments tested are considered contaminated = IL+. Dredged sediment will be loaded onto one or more designated material barge(s) for transport off-site for disposal at an appropriate upland facility. Some sediment is likely to be spilled grain, while other sediment appears to be the result of the three nearby combined storm outfalls, which discharge sediment and debris during rainfall events. Other sediment may have originated from surrounding areas which are not as deep, as a result of marine currents or tug wash. Anthropogenic debris in the area to be dredged includes steel pieces, a tire, and many small bits of garbage.

Document.project_name: Replacement and Repair of Utility Poles - Farnham Range and Training Area
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project for the replacement and repair of utility poles within the firing ranges and training areas of Farnham. The work involves cutting utility poles which have been greatly weakened by the presence of Pileated Woodpecker cavities. These poles will be cut at the height of the wires, and new poles will later be added close by to install new wires. The cut poles, with no electric wires, will remain in the same place. The work also includes filling the cavities on some of the remaining solid utility poles, to restore their structural integrity. All the preserved poles will be repaired by applying a foam formula (Polywater UPR) that will expand to fill the entire cavity. All the work will be carried out outside the migratory bird nesting period (September 1 to April 14). National Defence, Real Estate Operations Unit, will oversee the project.

Document.project_name: Sanitary Sewer Repairs - Phase 2
YHZ Halifax Stanfield International Airport – Underground Tank Removal
Document.description:
The project involves the removal of a 50,000 litre furnace oil underground storage tank (UST), including connected piping and associated equipment. The tank is no longer in use and will be emptied of any residual oil and vapors, as required, prior to removal. The tank and associated equipment will be removed and disposed of in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

The UST is located within a landscaped area along the west side of Bell Boulevard, opposite the air terminal building at Halifax Stanfield International Airport.

Following the tank removal, soil samples will be collected from the base and sidewalls of the tank excavation and submitted for laboratory analysis to assess soil quality. The excavation will be backfilled and the site re-instated following completion of the work. Clean fill from another area of the airport property may be used as required to complete backfilling.

The work is anticipated to take place from September 22 to September 25, 2026. Traffic control measures will be implemented as required to maintain public and worker safety during the work.

Document.project_name: Cedar LNG Project
Shoreline Protection - Whitby, Ontario
Document.proponent: Fisheries and Oceans Canada, Small Craft Harbours, Ontario & Prairie Region
Document.description:
Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) is proposing to install additional shoreline protection at Whitby Harbour. Clean rip rap stone will be used to repair and extend existing shoreline protection at two locations: the west (marina) side of the Yacht Club breakwater (#301) and the north side of the sawtooth breakwater (#602). A timber frame superstructure adjacent to the Yacht Club breakwater will be removed prior to the rock placement.  The total volume of stone required has not yet been confirmed.

The rip rap will be placed to match the existing shoreline alignment along the breakwater structures. Additional rock will also be placed in an upland swale adjacent to the south end of the Yacht Club parking lot.

Where feasible, mature trees within the project footprint will be relocated. Some shrubs and low-growing vegetation may need to be removed to accommodate the placement of rock.

The work is expected to be completed using heavy equipment, including rock trucks and an excavator operating from shore. Construction is anticipated to take approximately one to two weeks.

Document.project_name: Queen Elizabeth Driveway (QED) & Colonel By Drive (CBD) Active Transportation Improvements
location: Queen Elizabeth Driveway (QED) and Colonel By Drive (CBD)
Document.description:
The National Capital Commission (NCC) proposes a comprehensive active transportation improvement project along QED and CBD adjacent to the Rideau Canal in Ottawa, Ontario. These improvements will add unidirectional, physically separated summer-season bike lanes and a cycle track. The work will occur along QED between Preston Street and Laurier Avenue and along CBD between Hog's Back Road and Daly Avenue.

The project supports NCC policies to provide safer, continuous, sustainable mobility options and helps to separate pedestrians and cyclists. The NCC has reviewed areas where the space is tight or where cyclists and drivers often come into conflict. The project will address these challenges by creating continuous, easy-to-follow routes using separated bike lanes, shared-lane sections, and connections to nearby multi-use pathways.

The project is located entirely on NCC-owned federal lands. A Federal Land Use, Design and Transaction Approval (FLUDTA) is required under the National Capital Act. The NCC is the project sponsor and long-term steward of these parkways, with interests in mobility, safety, cultural landscape protection, and active use programming.

The scope of work will include but may not be limited to the following:


	Repair pavement and catch basins along the canal-side cycling lanes.
	Install new canal-side bike lanes with buffers and/or seasonal flexible delineator posts.
	Update pavement markings in tighter areas to create shared-lane segments.
	Build a 400-meter-long raised pathway along CBD between Laurier Bridge and Corktown Footbridge to improve accessibility and separation from traffic.
	Construct a retaining wall to support grade changes.
	Install entry and exit ramps between on-road and off-road cycling facilities.
	Install new signage.
	Review traffic speed limits.
	Plant new trees to compensate for the select removal of trees within the proposed new cycle track.


The QED and QBD corridors are a culturally significant landscape along the Rideau Canal UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is characterized by mature trees, multi-use pathways, and sloped embankments. There are multiple bridges and narrow roadway segments (Bank Street Bridge, Fifth Avenue, Pretoria Bridge, Bronson Bridge).

There are areas where soil quality exceeds certain federal or provincial guidelines; however, all soils are classified as non-hazardous. Any excess soil will be re-used or disposed of off-site in accordance with applicable regulations.

Construction will use standard equipment (excavators, pavers, rollers, graders, line-painting trucks). Construction is planned to begin in Summer 2026 and end in Spring 2027.  

The project's positive impacts include improved cyclist safety and mobility, fewer pedestrian–cyclist conflicts on crowded multi-use pathways and traffic calming through lane narrowing in select locations. During the work there are expected to be lane reductions, localized pathway detours, and construction noise/dust. The NCC will coordinate with the City of Ottawa to reduce traffic disruption during construction.

Document.project_name: Stormline Replacement
location: 1000 Airport Parkway Private, Ottawa, ON K1V 9B4
Document.description: The Ottawa International Airport Authority (OIAA) will be replacing the storm line headed west of the property to ensure the integrity of the stormwater system before the start of the 2026-2027 de-icing season. The project will also include the installation of new valves and an infiltration basin to better manage stormwater flows, reduce pressure on the system, and help prevent flooding during heavy rainfall and snowmelt events.

Document.project_name: Restoration of Watershed Subsystems in Welikanda DSD, Polonnaruwa District, Sri Lanka
location: Welikanda DSD, district Polonnaruwa, Sri Lanka
Document.description:
The ACCESS Sri Lanka Project, implemented by World Vision Lanka, includes watershed subsystem restoration activities within the Welikanda Divisional Secretariat Division (DSD) in Polonnaruwa District, Sri Lanka. The project aims to strengthen climate resilience, improve sustainable water resource management, and support agricultural livelihoods in local communities.

The physical activities include the rehabilitation of existing irrigation reservoirs, desilting of reservoirs and irrigation canals, repair of existing water management infrastructure, watershed restoration activities, erosion control measures, riparian vegetation restoration, and activities related to water resource management and protection.

Document.project_name: Repair of the Athletics Track - Royal Military College St-Jean, QC
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. The project involves renovating the athletics track which is in poor condition. The project will be carried out in several stages, including removing the existing rubber surface, rebuilding the track's infrastructure, installing an asphalt layer and a new rubber layer.

Document.project_name: Trigon Pacific LPG Project
Document.description: Trigon Pacific Terminals Ltd. is proposing to construct, operate, and decommission a new liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) storage and transload facility, located at the Port of Prince Rupert in British Columbia. As proposed, the Trigon Pacific LPG Project would include building up to 24 rail unloading racks to receive LPG, including propane and butane. LPG would be stored in tanks with a capacity of up to 158,000 m3 before being transferred to marine vessels for shipment to global markets. The project would involve developing an existing brownfield area and leverage existing infrastructure, including Trigon's existing jetty and LPG loading arms.

Document.project_name: New Southeast District Detachment
Document.description: The Southeast District Detachment will be a newly constructed building similar in size and function to the recently constructed St. Leonard Detachment. This new Detachment will allow for various units to be located in the same building, increasing overall effectiveness and efficiency, and will reduce the number of different leases by consolidating various office spaces including the current Southeast District Detachment, the Southeast District Policing Office (DPO), Major Crime Unit (MCU), Irishtown Detachment and Southeast District Courts Record Section. The project will provide current, up to date building and security standards to support RCMP investigative activities in the area of jurisdiction, while being able to better serve the community.  The project includes the acquisition of a new parcel of land.  Based on various operational requirements, it was determined that the optimal location for the new building would be in the vicinity of Salisbury, New Brunswick.

Document.project_name: Hydro One D6 Line Relocation– Garrison Petawawa
Document.description:
Hydro One's D6 transmission line requires relocation due to the existing transmission line corridor bisecting the increasingly active Ranges and Training Areas of Garrison Petawawa. The existing transmission line has also reached the end of its serviceability.

The project involves the preparations for, and installation of, single-circuit 115 kV wood or composite poled transmission line. Once completed, the new line transmission corridor will provide safe access to the line for maintenance, improve hydro reliability for the Ottawa Valley, support expanding Canada's Defence Operations and military residential housing development initiatives while minimizing impacts both to and by military activities.

Document.project_name: Soils Remediation – Garrison Petawawa
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. 4 Canadian Division Support Group (4 CDSG) Environment Services, Garrison Petawawa, is proposing the environmental-compliance driven remediation of contaminated soils in a graveled parking and vehicle/equipment storage compound directly south of 80 Montgomery Road (Building BB-130). Soils characterized as exceeding applicable Federal soil quality guidelines will be removed from the site to a licensed receiving facility.

Document.project_name: Bearskin Lake First Nation - Micro Subdivision Development
Document.description: Bearskin Lake First Nation is proposing the development of a micro subdivision. It will involve tree clearing, grubbing, grading construction of a 100 meter road access, service installations and extensions, and construction of the 18-lots. Each lot will have a footprint of approximately 500-700 meter squared (m2).

Document.project_name: Port of Botwood Wharf Rehabilitation Project
Document.ea_type: Early decision - No further assessment required
Document.description: Exploits Valley Port Corporation is proposing to revitalize infrastructure at the Port of Botwood marine terminal, located on the north shore of the Bay of Exploits in Newfoundland and Labrador. As proposed, the Port of Botwood Wharf Rehabilitation Project would replace deteriorated wharf infrastructure to accommodate ships up to 60,000 deadweight tonnage. The project would include the removal or stabilization of unsafe structural elements, the installation of new steel or concrete piles, upgrades to communication and safety systems, and the resurfacing of existing roads and laydown areas. The project would also require infilling to support wharf construction.

Document.project_name: McKay Brook Road Housing Development
Document.description: The project includes the construction of 4 housing lots, including the construction of 4, 1120sqft houses. Activities include clearing and grubbing of the lots - 4800m2 total (1200sqft each), construction of houses, connection into community water and wastewater services and landscaping.

Document.project_name: YUL Montreal-Trudeau International Airport – Air Canada parking in the Charlie NPSV sector
Document.description: Air Canada employee offices located in the domestic jetty have been relocated to a new building near the "Charlie" Non-Passenger and Vehicle Screening (NPSV) checkpoint. To facilitate access to these offices, allow employees to park nearby, and reduce the demand for shuttles, the existing parking lot next to the CNPV Charlie on Stuart-Graham Street South will be expanded to the north and south of the site. At the end of the project, the parking lot will have approximately 550 spaces and its expected lifespan is between 5 and 10 years.

Document.project_name: Installation of a Temporary Boiler and Fuel Storage Tank - Canadian Forces Base Halifax
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) has proposed a project to install and operate a temporary boiler and associated aboveground fuel storage tank to provide steam to Navy vessels alongside during periods when steam from the Central Heating Plant is not available (summer shut down, approximately May to October). The temporary boiler and fuel storage tank may be installed within 30 metres of the Halifax Harbour at various jetties depending on the operational requirement. Navy vessels may include any of the Halifax Class frigates, Marine Coast Defence Vessels, Arctic and Offshore Patrol Vessels, and others. The capacity of the fuel storage tank is not expected to exceed 2,500 litres.

Document.project_name: Peguis First Nation Interim Flood Protection Project
Document.description:
Peguis First Nation, Manitoba Infrastructure, and Indigenous Services Canada are developing an interim flood protection plan for Peguis First Nation. The purpose of the project is to protect homes and critical infrastructure until a long-term flood mitigation system is built. The interim plan includes the immediate construction of clay dikes around homes and a larger dike around key administrative, commercial, and cultural infrastructure, along with upgrades to local roads. Construction is targeted to begin in August 2026.

Project activities will include:


	Construction of a permanent central community dike around critical community buildings, as well as permanent subdivision dikes and individual dikes for homes most at risk of annual flooding.
	Raising on-reserve access roads where required.
	Developing, using, and reclaiming on-reserve borrow areas.
	Improving and maintaining haul routes where required.
	Completing drainage improvements.
	Clearing trees only where necessary.
	Developing temporary laydown and camp areas.


Peguis First Nation is the proponent and will provide oversight on the project, including local knowledge regarding the project area. Indigenous Services Canada is funding the work and will assist with any required on-reserve permits related to construction. Manitoba Transportation and Infrastructure will provide the technical expertise and resources needed to support planning, design, and construction.

All project work will take place on reserve, and some work will be located near the Fisher River. The Fisher River is considered a navigable watercourse within the project area. No in-water work or related in-water activities are planned. Borrow areas will not be located within 100 metres of the Fisher River or any other navigable watercourse; however, portions of individual and multi-property dikes may be within the two-year floodplain. For this reason, the project will be submitted to Fisheries and Oceans Canada for review to determine whether an authorization is required.

Document.project_name: Replacement of the St. Jean Garrison gas station
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. The project consists of removing seven underground storage tanks that have reached the end of their service life and replacing the old service station at the Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu Garrison with a new facility featuring two aboveground storage tanks, each with a capacity of 25,000 L.

Document.project_name: Binche Whut'en - Lift Station 1 Relocation
Reinforcement, Cleaning and Painting of Steel Components on Spans 1 to 3 of the Quebec Bridge (2026)
Document.proponent: The Jacques Cartier and Champlain Bridges Incorporated
Document.description:
The Quebec Bridge has connected Lévis and Quebec City since 1917. This multimodal structure provides active transportation users (pedestrians and cyclists), automobiles and trains with a means of crossing the St. Lawrence River. The Jacques Cartier and Champlain Bridges Incorporated (JCCBI), a federal Crown corporation, became the superficiary owner of the Quebec Bridge's structure in November 2024. Canadian National (CN) is the superficiary owner of the railway deck and the Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec (MTMD) is responsible for the roadway deck, including the sidewalk.

The objective of Contract 62778 is to carry out cleaning, preparation, reinforcement and painting work on steel components located on the south side of the Quebec Bridge. More specifically, the tasks and requirements associated with the work will include, without being limited to, the following:


	Reinforcement of steel components as well as cleaning and painting on certain sections of bracing under the deck of west cantilever span 3 and on the portal bracing
	Repair of a gusset on west anchor span 2
	Removal of the lighting system from the portal bracing on west anchor span 2
	Start of work in 2026 and completion by December 1 of the same year


Carrying out this work will require a number of partial or complete traffic closures that may be implemented during the day, at night, on weekends or for extended periods. When a complete closure is required, detour routes will be planned in collaboration with MTMD.

The project will integrate a set of environmental protective measure appropriate to this type of work, including measures to address the potential presence of peregrine falcons and their nests near work areas, as well as the management of construction methods to control contamination.

Document.project_name: Foundation Demolition and Associated Soil Remediation at Stony Point (former Camp Ipperwash), Ontario
location: Stony Point is located at 9356 Army Camp Road within the municipality of Lambton Shores.
Document.description:
Canada is committed to the timely and successful clearance and remediation of the Stony Point land in accordance with the Ipperwash Final Settlement Agreement between the Kettle and Stony Point First Nation and Her Majesty the Queen in Right of Canada. As per the Final Settlement Agreement, the Department of National Defence (DND) will conduct clearance and remediation activities to prevent, minimize and mitigate risks to human health, safety and the environment for the express purpose of making the land available for the use and benefit of the Kettle and Stony Point First Nation (KSPFN).

Although the Final Settlement Agreement requires all clearance and remediation activities to be conducted in accordance with the Clearance and Remediation Plan, there are interim activities that need to be completed to reduce health and safety risks and prepare the site for clean-up.

This project activity includes removal of the existing building foundations & slab on grades, thirty (30) in total and remediate the non-compliant soils at the Stony Point site and dispose at a licensed facility.

Document.project_name: Roberts Bank Terminal 2 Project
Document.ea_type: Environmental assessment by Review Panel under CEAA 2012
Document.description:
The Vancouver Fraser Port Authority proposes the construction and operation of a new three-berth marine container terminal located at Roberts Bank in Delta, British Columbia, approximately 35 km south of Vancouver. The proposed project, to be located next to the existing Deltaport and Westshore Terminals, would provide an additional 2.4 million twenty-foot equivalent units of container capacity per year at Roberts Bank.

Please note that the proponent was formerly known as Port Metro Vancouver.

Document.project_name: Kinistin Saulteaux Nation Road Improvements
Document.description:
Kinistin Saulteaux Nation is proposing to improve approximately 15 km of main access, rural residential, and core area roadways located throughout the community. The proposed project involves surfacing repairs, ditch grading improvements, embankment upgrades, and four culvert crossings.

Site preparation activities include stripping topsoil within roadway ditches of the core residential area where ditching upgrades will be completed, as well as the south side of the Highway 773 embankment where sloping improvements will be completed. Construction activities will consist of excavating and filling existing roadway surfacing to design elevations, excavation of roadway to facilitate culvert installations, preparing existing subgrade materials, and application of aggregate and surfacing materials to the road surface. Following construction, disturbed areas will be restored with topsoil and seeding.

All anticipated waste generated during construction activities will be managed and disposed of at designated landfill facility. Procedures will be implemented throughout construction to prevent potential contamination from petroleum products used for on-site equipment.

Document.project_name: Paqtnkek Subdivsion - Phase I
Document.description:
Proposed construction of a 11 lot subdivision at Paqtnkek-Niktuek IR 23, NS.

The project area is approximately 3 Ha and will service 11 housing lots. Activities during construction will include clearing, grubbing 300m of road construction, 345m of water main and 240m of gravity sewers to service the 11 lots. A pumping station and force main will be required for wastewater.
